piezas.titular: Codex fixed the wifi from the command line; a year on, ChatGPT operates the desktop
piezas.entradilla: In December 2025, people were celebrating an AI agent that solved a fault from the command line. A year on, that tool is in ChatGPT’s desktop app, which clicks and types in other programs.
cuerpo: On 2 December 2025, in Vibe Coding Educativo, someone described an unusual job given to Codex, OpenAI’s coding agent, in its command-line version (the window where text commands are typed). With administrator permissions, it had to find out why the internet connection kept dropping. It installed programs, ran tests and pinpointed the cause: an aluminium structure that was interfering with the wifi. Before, it was recalled, that would have meant long conversations with ChatGPT, copying its commands across. A Windows user replied that with PowerShell, its command line, you could do almost the same.

OpenAI brought [the Codex app](https://openai.com/index/introducing-the-codex-app/) to Windows on 4 March 2026 and on 9 July [merged it into the new ChatGPT desktop app](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-for-your-most-ambitious-work/), for Mac and Windows, with Codex on all plans, including the free one, according to the company. With its [computer use](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/computer-use) feature, it operates other apps by clicking and typing, and asks permission before using each one. In the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, it has been [available since 16 June](https://community.openai.com/t/now-in-europe-computer-use-the-codex-chrome-extension-personalized-memory-and-chronicle/1383925). Giving an agent full access still calls for care with students’ data, as [the paper reported on 3 November](pieza:2026-11-02/agentes-consola-acceso).
